overall_summary: Data shows clear audience inclination toward 'self respect' and modern digital relationship boundaries (chats, status lists, blue ticks) yielding the highest view counts (e.g., AfaLxMy6FMY at 40 views, rwOUYo_hayQ at 38 views), whereas pure abstract late-night rambling has underperformed.

winning_patterns.evidence: Shorts focusing on concrete phone actions like deleting chats or muting pinned chats (e.g., AfaLxMy6FMY, 0H4VygZ3DIU) consistently achieve higher views (30-40 range) compared to general loneliness.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks and stories around everyday smartphone UI moments (typing, deleting, viewing status lists).

winning_patterns.evidence: Audience responds better when the narrative shifts from passive suffering to active self-preservation or boundary setting.
winning_patterns.action: Continue utilizing the 'self respect' topic cluster with strong, decisive conclusions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing heavily on generic time references like 'रात के दो बजे' (G0gKV1p3ZHc) or 'चाय ठंडी हो गई' (uIbMpCjVutQ) had the lowest views (5-12 range).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid starting with weather, tea, or generic time stamps; anchor immediately to specific visual phone cues.
